summary: A Sporting News rumors tracker following free agent Shohei Ohtani's decision on where to sign after six seasons with the Angels. It collects dated reports from ESPN, The Athletic and MLB.com on teams like the Red Sox, Cubs, Mariners and Rangers, noting Ohtani wants to win and will sign the largest contract in baseball history. Teams have been told that publicly reported visits will be held against them, so news is scarce.
one_line: Running tracker of Nov. 2023 reports on where free agent Shohei Ohtani might sign, covering the Red Sox, Cubs, Mariners, Rangers and timing.
key_facts: Shohei Ohtani played his entire six-year MLB career with the Angels, whose teams never reached the postseason, and he will not be back.
The article says Ohtani will absolutely sign the largest contract in baseball history.
ESPN's Jeff Passan reported: "If visits between Ohtani and a team are reported publicly, it will be held against the team."
On Nov. 27, Passan wrote that the Red Sox might spend big on Ohtani, "who has an affinity for Boston."
Boston's backup plan includes prospects Roman Anthony, Marcelo Mayer and Kyle Teel, among the best trio of offensive prospects in baseball.
On Nov. 21, Rangers pitcher Max Scherzer said on Foul Territory, "Money's great, but winning's better."
On Nov. 20, Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reported Ohtani may be better off waiting for Yoshinobu Yamamoto to be posted, which triggers a 45-day negotiating window.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto is 25 and could command more than $200 million; a winter meetings deal in Nashville the first week of December would be ideal for MLB.
On Nov. 17, MLB.com's Daniel Kramer reported industry sources say landing Ohtani doesn't appear to be within the Mariners' realistic agenda this offseason.
Mariners appeal for Ohtani included young starting pitchers, Julio Rodriguez, his hero Ichiro, and offseason residence in Seattle.
On Nov. 16, ESPN's Jesse Rogers said the Cubs were one of seven finalists the first time, but the lack of an NL DH hurt then; the NL now has the DH.
The Cubs poached Craig Counsell from the rival Brewers to be their new manager.
On Nov. 11, Alden Gonzalez of ESPN reported Ohtani could sign before the Winter Meetings, which would let other teams pivot to targets like trading for Juan Soto.
